newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures pull back after see-saw trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures pull back after see-saw trade.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures pulled back from an earlier advance but ended Thursday with pared losses.
There was no new market-moving news and traders said the market remained vulnerable to further sharp swings on the back of fluctuating New York-listed arabica futures.
"Everybody is nervous. We are not sure where the market would go from here," said one.
The London market started off higher as expected and made further inroads on speculative buying. But origin price fixing and profit-taking at the peaks capped the advance.
Actively-traded May was chased up to a high of $1,635 a tonne before falling to a $1,550 floor as New York faltered after a higher start.
Traders said the slide in London accelerated after May triggered stop loss selling at below $1,580, the closing level on Wednesday.
Volume was a sizeable 11,686 lots. The nearby March/May and May/July switch was active, trading at $30-$35 and $20-$25 respectively.
Uncovered positions on spot March, which enters the first delivery day on Monday, continued to decline as origins continued price-fixing and players rolled forward positions.
By the close of business on Wednesday, the uncovered March position fell by 993 lots to 3,573. It stood at 5,459 lots at the start of the week.
New York's arabica futures finished Wednesday 9.60 cents up at 172.85 cents a lb after volatile trade.
